status: executable U(1) loop-equation plus Toeplitz-positivity hierarchy with converging plaquette bounds; finite-cutoff positive solutions remain nonunique and no 4D mass-gap certificate follows

model.measure: d mu_beta(theta)=exp(beta cos(theta)) dtheta/(2 pi I0(beta))
model.interpretation: one compact U(1) plaquette, equivalently the independent-plaquette building block of two-dimensional U(1) lattice gauge theory on a simply connected lattice

loopEquation.integrationByParts: 0=integral dtheta d/dtheta[sin(n theta) exp(beta cos(theta))] after trigonometric reduction
loopEquation.finiteCutoffConsequence: every retained moment is affine in u, but the loop equation alone leaves u free

positivityRelaxation.origin: for any coefficients c_i, c* T_K c=<|sum_i c_i exp(i i theta)|^2> >=0
positivityRelaxation.optimization: minimize and maximize u subject to T_K(u) positive semidefinite
expectedProperties: the exact Bessel ratio is feasible at every cutoff
lower bounds are nondecreasing and upper bounds are nonincreasing
the interval width decreases with loop cutoff
each finite cutoff admits a continuum of positive loop-equation solutions

finiteCutoffMultiplicity.statement: PSD of a truncated Toeplitz matrix constrains only positive trigonometric polynomials up to the retained degree; it does not guarantee that the recursively continued infinite sequence remains positive
finiteCutoffMultiplicity.spuriousWitnessRule: at each cutoff where possible choose a point strictly inside the K-feasible interval that violates positivity at K+1
finiteCutoffMultiplicity.meaning: finite loop equations plus positivity are relaxations, not uniqueness theorems

newComplexity: self-intersecting Wilson loops split into products and at finite N require multiple-trace variables
many geometrically distinct loops share a length cutoff
Hermitian, reflection and twist-reflection positivity give different semidefinite matrices
large-N factorization closes a different hierarchy from fixed SU(3)
fourDimensionalBoundary.massGapObservable: connected gauge-invariant correlators at increasing Euclidean time, not the one-plaquette expectation alone
fourDimensionalBoundary.requiredSupportStatement: a positive mass gap requires uniform exclusion of temporal spectral support near exp(-a Delta)=1
fourDimensionalBoundary.requiredLimits: loop cutoff and t_max to infinity, volume to infinity, and a to zero must be controlled uniformly
fourDimensionalBoundary.whyPlaquetteBoundsAreInsufficient: two-sided bounds on local Wilson loops can converge while arbitrarily small positive spectral weight remains at arbitrarily low energy

relationshipToPublishedBootstrap.largeN: Kazakov and Zheng combine Makeenko-Migdal equations, loop-length cutoffs and positivity to bound plaquettes in D=2,3,4 at SU(infinity)
relationshipToPublishedBootstrap.densityMatrix: Anderson and Kruczenski formulate positive Wilson-loop matrices from open paths and demonstrate strong finite-cutoff performance
relationshipToPublishedBootstrap.finiteSU3: Guo, Li, Yang and Zhu incorporate multiple traces and Hermitian/reflection/twist-reflection positivity to bound SU(3) plaquettes in D=2,3,4
relationshipToPublishedBootstrap.unclosedGate: these plaquette bounds do not yet give a regulator-uniform temporal spectral support exclusion proving the SU(3) mass gap

spin23Boundary.useful: loop positivity offers a gauge-invariant interface for testing any compact internal sector proposed alongside Spin(2,3)
spin23Boundary.notABridge: Spin(2,3) does not close the fixed-N Wilson-loop hierarchy or supply uniform temporal support bounds; spacetime symmetry cannot replace the compact gauge measure

decision: Wilson-loop bootstrap gives rigorous finite-cutoff bounds when loop equations are combined with positivity, but finite relaxations contain multiple and sometimes nonextendable positive solutions. Converged plaquette bounds are not a mass-gap proof; that requires temporal spectral support exclusion uniform in loop cutoff, time, volume and continuum limits.
